vulnerability_patterns.description: A 4-byte read could occur when only the starting offset was checked against section size, permitting the read to extend past the end of the section buffer.
trigger_conditions: `crc_offset` is less than section size but `crc_offset + 4` exceeds section size
`bfd_get_32(abfd, contents + crc_offset)` performs a 4-byte fetch from the computed offset
fix_patterns: Replace start-offset-only validation with full access-width bounds validation
Guard the read using `crc_offset + 4 > bfd_get_section_size(sect)` before dereferencing
evidence_lines: Comment states: `avoid reading off the end of the buffer.`

entry_points: Call sites performing fixed-width reads like `bfd_get_32(abfd, ptr + offset)`
suggestions: Model the width of consumer reads explicitly; a valid starting pointer is not proof that the whole read fits
Prefer detecting missing full-span bounds checks over simple offset-vs-size comparisons
Track aligned or adjusted offsets (`(crc_offset + 3) & ~3`) because post-processing can change safety conditions
Flag patterns where `offset >= size` guards precede multi-byte reads; require `offset + width <= size` semantics
Prefer consumer-side misuse detection at the read operation rather than only reasoning about prior string-length checks
Avoid using null/non-null or prior truncation by `strnlen` as proof that subsequent structured reads are in-bounds

shared_analysis.analysis_rationale: The patch tightens a bounds check in `bfd_get_section_size` usage inside `bfd_get_section_size`'s caller logic in `bfd/opncls.c` before `bfd_get_32 (abfd, contents + crc_offset)`. Previously it returned only when `crc_offset >= bfd_get_section_size (sect)`, which allowed reads starting within the section but extending 4 bytes past the end. The new guard `if (crc_offset + 4 > bfd_get_section_size (sect)) return NULL;` explicitly validates the full 4-byte read width, indicating a root-cause fix for reading beyond the available buffer, not merely a null or API issue.
